_note: Plain-English descriptors written AFTER fitting, from each component's top terms and highest-weighted passages. They are the author's reading of what the model grouped, not labels the model was given, and they stay provisional until two blinded reviewers score the topic-fit packet. Edit them only alongside the evidence that justifies the change.

topic_1.name: Executive and officer language
topic_1.reading: References to executives, officers, directors and the board. This component mixes two things rather than one: contractual executive-employment and change-in-control terms, and the officer or director language that appears in proxies and announcement press releases, including quoted remarks by a chief executive. Its internal coherence is the lowest of the three, which is what a mixed component looks like. It should not be read as a single kind of employee provision.

topic_2.name: Benefit plans and ERISA
topic_2.reading: Definitions and covenants about employee benefit plans: plan schedules, ERISA representations, pension and welfare arrangements, and undertakings about benefits after closing. This is the most self-consistent contractual component.

topic_3.name: Equity awards at the effective time
topic_3.reading: Treatment of stock, options, restricted stock and restricted stock units when the transaction closes: conversion, assumption, vesting and cash-out of outstanding awards. It is the most stable component, recovering in nearly every leave-one-deal-out fold.
